rubrics.justification: The response appropriately identifies a transfer-worthy expanded/full blastocyst, comments reasonably on ICM and TE visibility/quality, and notes intact zona without obvious degeneration. It is cautious about limitations of a single image, though some judgments about ICM/TE being less than textbook AA are somewhat subjective from this image.

It integrates maternal age, BMI, ovarian reserve markers, endometrial thickness, male-factor diagnosis, first-cycle status, and semen parameters well, and relates these factors to prognosis and embryo selection.

The reasoning is structured and internally consistent, with conclusions generally supported by morphology and clinical context. Minor overinterpretation exists around modest oocyte yield and possible overgrading from a single image, but overall logic is sound.

Recommendations are largely consistent with standard IVF practice: single embryo transfer in a young patient, routine luteal support, no bed rest, and avoiding unnecessary adjuvants. Slight deviations include speculative comments about grading discordance and broad statements about first-cycle prognosis.

Provides practical next steps for the current transfer and sensible future planning, including SET, luteal support, lifestyle advice, and when to consider further male-factor workup. Useful and specific, though not highly protocol-detailed.
